objective_for_doctor: A 29-year-old Male patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have chest pain even at rest, right side of the chest pain, and left side of the chest pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. I’m having chest pain at rest—both the right and left upper chest, kind of heavy and exhausting. I also get significantly sweaty and short of breath, and the pain goes to my left biceps/shoulder and even toward the thyroid cartilage, plus I feel epigastric pain.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent. When did the chest pain start, how long does each episode last, and do you feel it worsen with exertion or deep breathing? Also, do you have fever/cough, or any recent long travel/leg swelling?

It started very suddenly—like a fast onset (about 9/10). It’s happening right now at rest, and I’d say the pain is around 4/10 but very intense/heavy where it’s located (about 7/10). It gets worse with exertion, and I don’t have fever or cough. No recent long travel, and I don’t have leg swelling.

Doctor: I’m concerned about a heart-related cause given the sudden onset at rest with sweating, shortness of breath, and radiation to your shoulder/arm—can you tell me your age, any history of hypertension/diabetes/high cholesterol, smoking or drug use (especially cocaine), and whether you’ve had similar episodes? Also, right now, is your pain constant or coming in waves?

I’m 29. I have diabetes and high cholesterol, and I currently smoke cigarettes. I don’t have drug use like cocaine (I’m not using it). This is happening right now, and it feels like it’s constant/heavy rather than coming in waves.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute coronary syndrome (unstable angina / NSTEMI) likely—given sudden severe chest heaviness at rest with diaphoresis, shortness of breath, radiation to left shoulder/arm, plus diabetes, high cholesterol, and smoking.

[DDX]
1. Unstable angina
2. Stable angina
